question.text: If <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>4</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mi>i</mi></mrow></mfenced><mo>-</mo><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><mn>3</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>y</mi><mi>i</mi></mrow></mfenced><mo>=</mo><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo>-</mo><mn>5</mn><mi>i</mi></mrow></mfenced><mo>+</mo><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>y</mi><mi>i</mi></mrow></mfenced></math>, then the number of ordered pairs <math><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow></mfenced></math> is/are equal to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced open="{" close="}" separators="|"><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi>R </mi><mi mathvariant="normal">a</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">n</mi><mi>d </mi><msup><mi>i</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mfenced></math>

solution.text:
x4-3x2-3-1=0 & 2x-y+5-2y=0
x2-4x2+1=0 & 2x-3y+5=0
⇒x=2 or -2 & 2x-3y+5=0
When x=2,y=3 and when x=-2,y=13
⇒x,y=2,3 & -2,13
⇒ Number of ordered pair of x,y is equal to 2
